ops.title: yasyf-home FP bridge outage 2026-07-14: acct-12..16 EDEADLK, retreated to symlink
ops.body:
**Symptom.** Claude Code on yasyf-home (ccp v0.53.0, app cask 0.52.0, macOS 26.4.1) failed to read `~/.cc-pool/accounts/acct-13/settings.json` with EDEADLK. All six hostsync-materialized FP accounts (acct-11..16, created Jul 13 22:11–22:12 during the origin-owned-sync migration) had `SF_DATALESS` content; enumeration worked, materialization failed instantly. acct-11 appeared healthy only because a 02:38 session had fully hydrated it — zero dataless files left.

**Timeline.**
- Jul 13 22:08:32 — daemon (fresh v0.53.0) logs `file provider bridge: socket …/Group Containers/SXKCTF23Q2.ccp/b.sock did not come up within 3s`.
- Jul 13 22:12:35–36 — TCC `kTCCServiceSystemPolicyAppData` rows written for `/Users/yasyf/.cc-pool/bin/cc-pool` + Cellar/0.53.0 (auth_value 5, auth_reason 2); one second later `bridge v0.53.0 started; socket=…/b.sock … is up`. Bridge serves overnight; acct-11 hydrates at 02:38.
- Jul 14 04:21:02 — `file provider companion app is down; launching /Applications/CCPoolStatus.app in the background`. From the next session start (04:44, select → acct-13) every materialization fails EDEADLK **even though the daemon still held b.sock** — the bridge wedged daemon-side when the app died.
- 04:59 `ccp fp repair --account 13` (re-register): no effect on reads.
- 05:01+ daemon restarts (brew services): bind of b.sock now fails reproducibly with the "awaiting app-group-container consent" message despite the TCC rows existing and the SSH user being able to write in the group container. App bounce + `ccp fp onboard` didn't recover it: onboard spins at "waiting for the CCPoolStatus app to come up" even while the app (pid alive) serves `~/.cc-pool/domains.sock`.

**Remediation applied (one-off, machine-level).** `ccp fp repair --retreat --account N` for N=13,12,14,15,16 — the designed symlink-floor escape hatch. Safe here: those five accounts were 100% dataless (nothing local to lose) and session-free apart from acct-13's already-wedged claude. All six accounts read OK after; acct-11 left on FP (live sessions, fully hydrated). First new session (05:12:27, cc-steer → acct-14) ran normally.

**Open code-side questions for the fix in flight** (parallel agent owns):
1. Why does the daemon's b.sock bind fail under launchd when TCC AppData rows exist for the exact stable path — and why did it wedge (serving but dead) rather than fail loud when the companion app died at 04:21? The consent-hint log message misdiagnoses at least one failure mode.
2. `select` happily routes new sessions to credential-less, never-hydrated accounts (acct-13 at 04:44/04:53 despite doctor's "no credential in either backend"); "acct-13 auth recovered; needs-login cleared" at 00:27 looks like the needs-login clear bug.
3. `ccp fp onboard`'s app probe disagrees with reality (app up + serving domains.sock, probe spins). Also `ccp fp repair` (re-register) can't help when the bridge itself is down — consider a bridge-health rung in its verdict.

**Residual state on yasyf-home.** acct-12..16 parked on symlink with pending user browser-logins; migrate back to FP (`ccp migrate --to fileprovider`) only after the bridge fix ships. acct-11 still FP-backed with the bridge down: reads fine (hydrated), but provider-upstream sync/new-file serving is queued until the bridge is fixed. Daemon also loops `deferring stranded-bridge heal` on acct-01/02/07/10 (live sessions) — pre-existing, untouched.
